title: Finding FB2-REV-FND-000003: safety requirement has no verifies/validates link (FB2-SAF-FSR-000002, profile as_is)
lifecycle_status_note: 'draft': this record makes the validator's standing finding legible and dispositioned. It does not close the condition. No human reviewer has confirmed it, and human approval of the artifact it describes remains 'pending'.

revision_history.author: quality_engineer
revision_history.description: First-class record of the standing validator finding 'safety requirement has no verifies/validates link' raised against FB2-SAF-FSR-000002 in profile as_is. Transcribed from the validator, not paraphrased.

validator_rule: corpus.py _validate_links semantic pass: verified = {l['source_id'] for l in links if l.get('relation_type') in ('verifies','validates')}; raise if a safety-domain requirement's id is absent from that set.
validator_finding_verbatim: safety requirement has no verifies/validates link
evidence: Validator finding verbatim: 'safety requirement has no verifies/validates link'. Measured against the registry: Link census measured on the registry: verifies links run TMS->FSR (15), TMS->SWR (10), TMS->TSR (7); validates links run TMS->SCO (1), TMS->SGO (1). In the corpus's own convention a test measure is the SOURCE and the requirement is the TARGET, so a well-verified requirement appears as a link TARGET, never as a source. FB2-SAF-FSR-000002 in profile as_is is the target of at least one TMS->FSR verifies link, but is not the SOURCE of any verifies or validates link, which is what the rule tests. The requirement text is (SOA limit monitoring, debounce 2-in-100 ms, classify within 5 ms), and it is a functional safety requirement with an engineering_domain of safety, so the rule applies to it.
impact: The literal statement 'has no verifies/validates link' is only partly accurate for this artifact. Verification traceability to this requirement demonstrably exists in the corpus, because test measures verify it; what does not exist is a link in the direction the rule inspects. A reader who trusts the finding literally would conclude the requirement is unverified and go looking for missing test evidence that is in fact present. A reader who dismisses the finding as a rule artefact would dismiss it for the security requirements too, where no such link exists in either direction and the conclusion would be wrong.
root_cause: The rule tests only the SOURCE side of a verifies/validates relation, while the corpus's link convention places the test measure at the source and the requirement at the target. Under that convention the rule cannot be satisfied by any requirement that is verified in the corpus's own idiom, so it fires on every safety requirement that has a test. The rule is not wrong to exist - it is the MUT mutation detector for a missing verification link - but its firing on a well-verified requirement is a direction mismatch between the rule and the registry convention, not a traceability defect.
resolution: NOT RESOLVED. The check is deliberately left unchanged: relaxing it would suppress a genuine detector that the corpus needs for its mutation scenarios. The correct fix is a decision about link-direction convention, and it belongs to the corpus owner and the schema owner jointly, not to a finding record. Until that decision is taken this finding stands for every safety requirement, and the honest reading for a reviewer is: verification links must be examined on BOTH sides before concluding that a safety requirement is unverified.
